name: befunge93
why: A two-dimensional esoteric language where code flows in a grid and the program edits itself, a classic mind-bending detour.

brief.what_it_is: Befunge-93 is an esoteric programming language by Chris Pressey, from 1993. A program is a fixed-size grid of ASCII characters, each generally one instruction, and the instruction pointer can travel in any of the four cardinal directions across that grid, not just left to right. The pointer starts in the upper-left corner moving right and keeps moving in its current direction until an instruction changes it. Data lives on a stack, and the p instruction can write into the grid, so programs can rewrite their own code. The packaged tool is the reference interpreter bef, which the catseye listing gives as ANSI C under a BSD license. I did not read bef's own documentation, so I cannot confirm its exact input or output handling beyond that.
brief.why_it_exists: Pressey's stated goal, per the esolangs.org entry, was to create a language that was as difficult to compile as possible. The catseye listing presents it as one of his more popular languages, and says it begat Befunge-97, Funge-98 and Wierd.
brief.how_it_works: Execution is driven by a program counter (called an instruction pointer in Befunge-98) that moves across the playfield with inertia until an instruction changes its direction. Control flow is done by steering the pointer through arrows and conditional direction instructions such as horizontal and vertical IF. Stack operations and the g and p instructions read and write the grid by coordinate, which is what makes the code self-modifying.
brief.install_notes: Nothing beyond the brew install was described in the pages I read. The catseye listing names the reference implementation as bef, written in ANSI C with a BSD license. The brew metadata lists executables bef, bef2c and befprof, but I saw no usage text or install steps for any of them.
brief.standout: The language is built to resist compilation: code can rewrite itself, and the same instruction can run in four different directional contexts. That makes it a different kind of puzzle from ordinary left-to-right languages, and the esolangs.org entry notes that compilers for it have still been written.
brief.status: Unknown as to current maintenance. The catseye listing marks Befunge-93 development-stage as mature and lists the bef reference implementation under BSD, but I saw no release date or recent commit in either page. The language itself dates from September 1993.
brief.caveats: The catseye and esolangs pages describe a compiler called bf2c, while the brew formula lists bef2c, so the name may differ between sources. befprof appears in the brew formula but in nothing I read. The esolangs.org page says the bf2c compiler does not handle p correctly. The reference -93 playfield is limited to 80x25 cells. I did not read the bef README, so build and platform details are unverified. Both pages were truncated by the fetch tool, but the Befunge-93 entries were within the portion returned.
quotes: One of the more popular languages I ever designed and implemented.

Befunge-93 is an esoteric programming language where the program exists in a two-dimensional grid of cells, where each cell contains a single instruction, and execution can proceed in any cardinal direction across this grid
